'''''Trifolium occidentale''''', the '''western clover''', is a [[clover]] plant belonging to the genus ''[[Trifolium]]'' in the legume family, [[Fabaceae]].

This species lives almost exclusively in [[dune|sand dunes]] and sea cliffs on the Atlantic coast of Europe, especially [[Cornwall]] and the [[Channel Islands]].

==Description==
''Trifolium occidentale'' is a [[perennial]] herb. It is [[self-compatible]], [[diploid]], and [[stoloniferous]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gibson |first1=Pryce B. |last2=Beinhart |first2=George |year=1969 |title=Hybridization of ''Trifolium accidentale'' With Two Other Species of Clover |journal=[[Journal of Heredity]] |volume=60 |issue=2 |pages=93–96 |doi=10.1093/oxfordjournals.jhered.a107944 |url=http://jhered.oxfordjournals.org/content/60/2/93.extract|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="CanadaCanada1986">
{{cite journal |last1=Parrott |first1=W.A. |last2=Smith |first2=R.R. |year=1986 |title=Evidence for the existence of endosperm balance true clovers ''(Trifolium'' Spp.) |journal=Canadian Journal of Genetics and Cytology |volume=28 |pages=581–586 |doi=10.1139/g86-085 |url=http://mulch.cropsoil.uga.edu/~parrottlab/Publications/ParrottandSmith1986b.pdf}}</ref> Its flowers are white, similar to [[white clover]] (''Trifolium repens''), with which it has long been confused.

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described in 1961 by Dr [[David E Coombe]] of [[Cambridge University]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Coombe |first=D.E. |year=1961 |title=''Trifolium occidentale'', a new species related to ''T. repens'' L. |journal=Watsonia |volume=5 |pages=68–87}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is found only within {{Convert|100|m}} of the coast, in western Europe. It inhabits sandy [[Dune|dunes]],<ref name="Biologiczna1997">{{cite journal |last=Kazimierska |first=Ewa M. |year=1997 |title=Male sterility and its inheritance in ''Trifolium occidentale'' Coombe |journal=Acta Biologica Cracoviensia, Series Botanica
 |volume=39 |issue=Suppl |pages=18 }}</ref> including dune and dry short coastal grasslands and sea cliffs, especially around rock outcrops.<ref name="BRC">{{cite web|url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/trifolium-occidentale|title=Trifolium occidentale (Western Clover)|publisher=Online Atlas of British and Irish Flora|access-date=13 April 2012}}</ref> Its range extends from the east coast of [[Ireland]] and the southern British Isles such as [[Cornwall]], the [[Channel Islands]] and [[Isle of Scilly]] in particular, to the northwest of the [[Iberian Peninsula]], although much less common. In France, it is found on the shores of the [[Armorican Massif]] and [[Normandy]] and [[Brittany]].

It was discovered in Ireland in June 1979 and in Wales in 1987.<ref name="BRC" /> In Ireland it is found "at intervals along the coast from [[Skerries, County Dublin|Skerries]] in north [[County Dublin]] to [[Forlorn Point]], [[County Wexford]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ackeroyd |first=J.R. |year=1983 |title=Further Notes on ''Trifolium occidentale'' D. E. Coombe in Ireland |journal=The Irish Naturalists' Journal |volume=21 |issue=1 |pages=32–34 |jstor=25538682}}</ref> It is most common on the Cornish coast. It closely resembles the white clover but appears earlier in the season and is more compact, and the leaves are more opaque, often a blue-green.<ref name="WB">{{cite web|url=http://web.guernsey.net/~cdavid/botany/files/trifolium%20occidentale/index.html|title=Trifolium occidentale|publisher=Web.guernsey.net|access-date=13 April 2012}}{{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
